texts.facts: The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:- On 11.7.1997 at 11 a.m., PW1, the Food Inspector purchased 750 gram of green gram dhall from the shop of the first accused. The s econd accused was the manufacturer of the said shop. After sampling as per rules, one sample was sent to the Public Analyst for analysis. The Public Analyst after analysis submitted Ext.P10 report stating that the sample contained synthentic Food colour tartrazine and was therefore adulterated under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules. Thereafter, on the request of the accused, the second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis. Ext . P12 report of the Central Food Laboratory would also show that the sample did not conform to the standard of split moong dhall as per the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules and was therefore adulterated. 4. Before the trial Court, PW1 and PW2 were examined and Exts.P1 to P18 were marked for the prosecution. CW1 was examined as court witness. DW1 was examined for the revision petitioner. 5. After evaluating the evidence, the court below acquitted the revision petitioner for the charge of adulteration. Since Ext.P12 report showed that the sample contained tartrazine, the sample was misbranded as contended by the complainant. In the complaint, the complainant contended that the sample was adulterated and misbranded on the reason that it contained the synthetic colour tartrazine, as the Public Analyst report would reveal so. It is borne out from the records that it is only from Exts.P10 and P12 reports that the sample contained tartrazine and it was only because of that, the court found that the sample was misbranded. S.Ramaswamy vs The State Of Kerala on 14 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176000630/ 2 6.
texts.arguments: The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has argued that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext.P12 report cannot be acted upon to hold that the sample was misbranded or adulterated. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument. A Division Bench of this Court in judgment dated 17-11-2015 in Crl.M.C. No. 417 of 2011 held that the decision in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) is applicable to all cases.

The learned counsel for the revision petitioner relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument.
